summary: SSE resume hides conditional terminal 'end' event after edge proxy connection migration
description:
Issue summary: Multiple customers (first reported by NimbusChat) observe that when an SSE session is interrupted by an edge proxy connection migration and then resumes, the final conditional 'end' control event that signals a clean terminal block is not delivered to the client. Impact: Final punctuation/closing JSON wrapper for streamed choices is missing or truncated, causing client parsers to treat the response as incomplete. Affected clients see partial final choices, missing closing metadata and inconsistent 'done' flags.

Environment: prod/us-east fronted by our edge-proxy fleet; customers on enterprise plan using our JS SDK with fetch-based SSE. Affected models: redwood-alpha-1 and gpt-open-7b observed in reproductions.

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Start a long SSE stream via the JS SDK (example attached) for a request that emits a conditional 'end' control event once model completes.
2) Trigger a controlled edge-proxy connection migration (simulated by tcpkill / forced circuit shuffle on repro host) during the last 5–10s of streaming.
3) Allow client to auto-reconnect and resume session using resume-token.
4) Observe that stream payload contains final text tokens but final 'end' control event and trailing metadata are missing or arrive as an empty line.

Observed behavior: Clients receive what looks like the last paragraph but no terminal control event; JSON wrappers may be unterminated (missing closing ']' or '}}'). Some SDKs treat this as stream timeout and throw parsing errors. No 5xx seen in logs; the runtime marks the session as Completed, but the edge-proxy logs show an early 101->200 handoff.

Expected behavior: Resume should preserve and forward the terminal 'end' control event and associated metadata so clients can deterministically close the stream.

Attachments: repro script, client traces, edge-proxy logs excerpt, sample SSE transcript (redacted), sample SDK stacktrace.
comments: Aisha Karim (Support) - 2026-03-10: Opened ticket after NimbusChat sent multiple example transcripts showing missing terminal control event. Included repro steps and raw SSE transcript.

Jonah Park (Eng) - 2026-03-10: Assigned. Initial hypothesis: edge-proxy connection migration is normalizing or dropping a one-byte terminal marker during handoff. Will reproduce in staging with tcpkill and enable verbose edge-proxy debug logs.

NimbusChat (Customer) - 2026-03-10: Customer indicates this happens intermittently, ~3% of long streams, higher when mobile clients are on flaky networks. They can repro with our sample app by toggling airplane mode twice.

Samir Patel (SRE) - 2026-03-11: Correlated incidents to an edge-proxy host rotation cluster at 2026-03-09T23:xxZ in us-east-1. Found sequences where proxied response flush was acknowledged but the control frame arrived in a subsequent TLS record that was dropped during rebind.

Jonah Park (Eng) - 2026-03-12: Added temporary mitigation to SDK to accept final newline-empty-line as implicit end and attempt JSON reassembly. This is a conservative workaround; customers must upgrade SDK to opt-in. Preparing runtime patch to include redundant end marker during resume window.
investigation_notes: Reproduction: Created a long streaming request that emits final 'end' control event and reproduction succeeded locally when inducing connection migration using tc qdisc netem + tcpkill. Edge-proxy logs: observed sequence of events where TLS connection handoff returned 200 before last TLS record with control event arrived. Packet capture (pcap) shows last Application DATA record containing "\n[end]'" was retransmitted but ACKed only to previous connection; forwarded handover created a small window where last record was not consumed. Runtime behavior: serving-runtime set session state to COMPLETED when it sent terminal event; however, the edge-proxy's resume logic used idempotency mapping that filtered duplicate control frames during rebind, treating them as retransmits and dropping the trailing control marker. Hypotheses: 1) Edge-proxy idempotency filter incorrectly dedupes final control markers when resume-token timestamp delta < 1s. 2) SDK resume handshake does not include a trailing-offset/byte-check and relies solely on token; missing offset allows proxy to drop trailing bytes during handoff. Evidence: grep of edge-proxy logs found markers 'idemp:drop control-frame end token=<token>' at the time of incidents. Repro commands: curl --http2 -N -H 'Accept: text/event-stream' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams?resume_token=abc ; tcpdump -w capture.pcap host <edge> and filter for TLS records containing [end]. Observed commit: https://github.com/redwood-inference/edge-proxy/commit/8f3b2d5 (added logging). Next steps: instrument edge-proxy to preserve last 2 control frames during connection migration, add resume offset to SDK handshake, and add runtime idempotency blacklist for 'end' markers during resume window.
resolution: Mitigation deployed: 2026-03-12 - Released edge-proxy logging and temporary config to preserve last 2 control frames during connection migration in the us-east canary. SDK patch 1.2.4 published to treat an empty final event as implicit end; provided NimbusChat with pre-release build. Long-term fix: engineering to ship edge-proxy change that disables dedupe for 'end' control events within a 2s resume window and update resume handshake to include byte-offset verification. Follow-up tasks: test rollout across eu-west and production runbook to validate resume integrity (INT- follow-up ticket created). Customer follow-up: NimbusChat asked for post-rollout verification; Support scheduled a joint test on 2026-03-15. Ticket status: In Progress until full prod rollout confirmed.
